parsedVerdict.reasoning:
ListProjectTasksUseCase does normal application-layer work. It runs the use case: it checks the project exists through the ProjectRepository port, asks the TaskRepository port for tasks with filters, and maps domain Task entities to TaskOutput DTOs. It contains no persistence code, no HTTP or framework handling, and no domain business rules. Task status comes from task.getStatus(), which stays in the domain.

One small smell: execute throws ApplicationError("project not found", 404). The number 404 is an HTTP status code, and mapping errors to transport status codes belongs in the infrastructure layer (for example TaskController). A neutral code would be cleaner. This is not counted as a violation because the call only tags the error with a value, contains no transport logic, and uses an error type defined in the application layer.
